content:
Many people have criticized Apple's designs in recent years as having lost some of their signature whimsy. Well, here's the latest example of the tide seemingly turning.

Apple has tucked an homage to classic Mac OS into the Settings app of iOS 27: Clarus the Dogcow. Here's how to trigger it……

iOS 27 also adds the ability for users to customize the strength of the Liquid Glass transparency effect, with a slider ranging from "fully transparent" to "fully dark." You can find this setting in Settings → Display & Brightness → Liquid Glass.

Within the page, Apple has added a mock website UI that lets you preview the appearance of Liquid Glass as you adjust the slider. There's a tiny scrollable region with some text and a photo of Apple Park.

And here's the Easter egg: scroll all the way to the bottom, and then keep swiping up with your finger, and a photo of a Clarus the Dogcow plushy appears next to the pond at Apple Park. Rainbow text reading "Moof!" (the sound a Dogcow makes) shows up in the sample search text field as well.

If you type "Moof!" into Siri in Spotlight, it will also reply "Nice dogcow."

For those unfamiliar with the history, Clarus the Dogcow dates back to an icon created by Susan Kare for the original Mac, as a character in the Cairo font (the icon font of the classic Mac OS, similar to Windows' Dingbats). It doesn't really serve any functional purpose beyond being a fun little Easter egg.

You can find the same Easter egg in the macOS Golden Gate System Settings app, under Display & Brightness.
